questions.question: The radius of a wire is decreased to one – third. If volume remains the same, length will increase by
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a wire is decreased to one – third. If volume remains the same, length will increase by
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a wire (cylinder), volume V = πr2l. If volume remains constant, l ∝ 1/r2.

Given the radius is decreased to 1/3, the new radius factor is 1/3.

The square of the radius factor is (1/3)2 = 1/9.

Since length is inversely proportional to r2, the length must be multiplied by the reciprocal of 1/9, which is 9.

∴ The correct answer is 9 times.

Alternate Method

Given:

Original radius = r

New radius (r′) = r/3

Original volume (V1) = New volume (V2)

Formula Used:

Volume of a cylinder (wire) = πr2l, where r is the radius and l is the length.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the original length be l and the new length be l′.

⇒ V1 = π × r2 × l

⇒ V2 = π × (r/3)2 × l′

⇒ V2 = π × (r2/9) × l′

⇒ Since V1 = V2:

⇒ π × r2 × l = π × (r2/9) × l′

⇒ l = l′ / 9

⇒ l′ = 9 × l

∴ The correct answer is 9 times.

Additional Information

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume is given by V = πr2h, where r is the base radius and h is the height or length.

Relationship between Dimensions

When volume is constant, the ratio of lengths is inversely proportional to the ratio of the squares of the radii: l1 / l2 = (r2 / r1)2.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The surface area of the side of the wire is 2πrl. In this problem, the CSA changes by a factor of (1/3) × 9 = 3 times.

questions.question: In a trapezium ABCD, AB and CD are parallel sides and ∠ ADC = 90°. If AB = 15 cm, CD = 40 cm and diagonal AC = 41 cm. Then the area of the trapezium ABCD is
questions.questionHtml: In a trapezium ABCD, AB and CD are parallel sides and ∠ ADC = 90°. If AB = 15 cm, CD = 40 cm and diagonal AC = 41 cm. Then the area of the trapezium ABCD is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In right-angled triangle ADC, using Pythagorean triplet (9, 40, 41):

Height (AD) = √(AC2 − CD2) = √(412 − 402) = √81 = 9 cm.

Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Area = 1/2 × (15 + 40) × 9 = 27.5 × 9 = 247.5 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 247.5 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Parallel sides AB = 15 cm and CD = 40 cm.

Diagonal AC = 41 cm and ∠ADC = 90°.

Formula Used:

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

Pythagoras Theorem: h2 + base2 = hypotenuse2

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔADC, ∠D = 90°

⇒ AD2 + CD2 = AC2

⇒ AD2 + 402 = 412

⇒ AD2 = 1681 − 1600

⇒ AD2 = 81

⇒ AD = √81 = 9 cm

⇒ Since AB || CD and ∠ADC = 90°, AD is the height (h) of the trapezium.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (AB + CD) × AD

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (15 + 40) × 9

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 55 × 9

⇒ Area = 27.5 × 9 = 247.5 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 247.5 cm2.

Additional Information

Properties of a Right Trapezium

A right trapezium has at least two adjacent right angles. The height is equal to the length of the non-parallel side perpendicular to the bases.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (9, 40, 41), (3, 4, 5), and (8, 15, 17) help solve geometry problems quickly without full calculation of squares.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (mid-segment) connects the midpoints of non-parallel sides and its length is the average of the parallel sides: m = (a + b) / 2.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus having one side 10 cm and one diagonal 12 cm is
questions.questionHtml: The area of a rhombus having one side 10 cm and one diagonal 12 cm is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other at 90° forming right-angled triangles.

Half of the given diagonal = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm and Side = 10 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (6, 8, 10), the other half-diagonal must be 8 cm.

Second diagonal (d2) = 8 × 2 = 16 cm.

Area = 1/2 × d1 × d2 = 1/2 × 12 × 16 = 96 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 96 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side (a) = 10 cm

One diagonal (d1) = 12 cm

Formula Used:

Area of Rhombus = 1/2 × d1 × d2

Relation between side and diagonals: a2 = (d1/2)2 + (d2/2)2

Calculations:

⇒ 102 = (12/2)2 + (d2/2)2

⇒ 100 = 62 + (d2/2)2

⇒ 100 = 36 + (d2/2)2

⇒ (d2/2)2 = 100 − 36 = 64

⇒ d2/2 = √64 = 8 cm

⇒ d2 = 8 × 2 = 16 cm

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 12 × 16

⇒ Area = 6 × 16 = 96 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 96 cm2.

Additional Information

Diagonal and Side Relationship

The relationship between the side (a) and the two diagonals (d1 and d2) is given by 4a2 = d12 + d22.

Properties of Rhombus

All four sides are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°). Diagonals also bisect the interior angles of the rhombus.

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter of a rhombus is calculated as 4 × side (a).

questions.question: The cost of levelling a circular field at 50 Paise per square metre is Rs. 7700. The cost (in Rs) of putting up a fence all round it at Rs. 1.20 per meter is (Use π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The cost of levelling a circular field at 50 Paise per square metre is Rs. 7700. The cost (in Rs) of putting up a fence all round it at Rs. 1.20 per meter is (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of field = Total levelling cost ÷ Rate = 7700 ÷ 0.50 = 15400 m2.

Standard Circle Property: If Area = 154, Radius = 7 and Circumference = 44.

Since Area = 154 × 100, then Radius = 7 × 10 = 70 m and Circumference = 44 × 10 = 440 m.

Total Fencing Cost = Circumference × Rate = 440 × 1.20 = ₹528.

∴ The correct answer is ₹528.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of levelling = ₹7700

Rate of levelling = 50 Paise per m2 = ₹0.50 per m2

Rate of fencing = ₹1.20 per metre

Formula Used:

Area of a circle = πr2

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the field = Total levelling cost ÷ Levelling rate

⇒ Area = 7700 ÷ 0.50 = 15400 m2

⇒ πr2 = 15400

⇒ (22/7) × r2 = 15400

⇒ r2 = (15400 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r2 = 700 × 7 = 4900

⇒ r = √4900 = 70 m

⇒ Circumference of the field = 2 × π × r

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 70

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 10 = 440 m

⇒ Cost of fencing = Circumference × Fencing rate

⇒ Cost of fencing = 440 × 1.20 = ₹528

∴ The correct answer is ₹528.

Additional Information

Standard Circle Values (for π = 22/7)

If r = 7, then Circumference = 44 and Area = 154. If radius is multiplied by 'k', circumference is multiplied by 'k' and area by 'k'2.

Relationship between Cost and Dimension

Cost of Levelling = Area × Rate per unit area. Cost of Fencing = Perimeter (Circumference) × Rate per unit length.

Area in terms of Circumference

Area = C2 ÷ (4π), where C is the circumference of the circle.

questions.question: The radius of a cylindrical milk container is half its height and total surface area of the inner part is 616 sq.cm. The amount of milk that the container can hold, approximately, is [Use : √5 = 2.23 and π = 22/7]
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a cylindrical milk container is half its height and total surface area of the inner part is 616 sq.cm. The amount of milk that the container can hold, approximately, is [Use : √5 = 2.23 and π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio given: r = h ÷ 2 ⇒ h = 2r.

Inner surface area (open top) = πr2 + 2πrh = 5πr2.

5 × (22/7) × r2 = 616 ⇒ r2 = 39.2.

r = √39.2 = 14 ÷ √5 = 14 ÷ 2.23 ≈ 6.28 cm.

Volume = πr2h = (22/7) × 39.2 × (2 × 6.28) ≈ 1547 cm3 ≈ 1.547 litres.

∴ The correct answer is 1.53 litres.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = h ÷ 2 ⇒ Height (h) = 2r

Total Surface Area (Inner) = 616 cm2

π = 22/7, √5 = 2.23

Formula Used:

Inner TSA of open cylinder = Area of base + Curved Surface Area = πr2 + 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ TSA = πr2 + 2πr(2r) = πr2 + 4πr2 = 5πr2

⇒ 5 × (22/7) × r2 = 616

⇒ (110/7) × r2 = 616

⇒ r2 = (616 × 7) ÷ 110 = 5.6 × 7 = 39.2

⇒ r = √39.2 = √(196 ÷ 5) = 14 ÷ √5

⇒ r = 14 ÷ 2.23 ≈ 6.278 cm

⇒ h = 2 × 6.278 = 12.556 cm

⇒ Volume (V) = πr2h = (22/7) × 39.2 × 12.556

⇒ V = 123.2 × 12.556 = 1546.89 cm3

⇒ Capacity in litres = 1546.89 ÷ 1000 ≈ 1.547 litres

⇒ Closest option is 1.53 litres.

∴ The correct answer is 1.53 litres.

Additional Information

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder is given by V = πr2h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh. Total Surface Area (TSA) of a closed cylinder = 2πr(r + h).

Capacity Conversion

1 litre = 1000 cm3 or 1000 millilitres. For calculations in litres, divide the volume in cm3 by 1000.

Open vs Closed Containers

For an open-top container, the surface area is base area + curved area (πr2 + 2πrh), whereas a closed one includes two circular bases (2πr2 + 2πrh).

questions.question: The sum of the length and breadth of a rectangle is 6 cm. A square is constructed such that one of its sides is equal to a diagonal of the rectangle. If the ratio of areas of the square and rectangle is 5 : 2, the area of the square in cm 2 is
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the length and breadth of a rectangle is 6 cm. A square is constructed such that one of its sides is equal to a diagonal of the rectangle. If the ratio of areas of the square and rectangle is 5 : 2, the area of the square in cm<sup>2</sup> is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of sides (L + B) = 6 ⇒ (L + B)2 = 36 ⇒ L2 + B2 + 2LB = 36.

Ratio of Areasquare : Arearect = (L2 + B2) : LB = 5 : 2.

Let L2 + B2 = 5x and LB = 2x.

Substitute in expansion: 5x + 2(2x) = 36 ⇒ 9x = 36 ⇒ x = 4.

Area of square = L2 + B2 = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 20 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of length (L) and breadth (B) = 6 cm

Side of square (s) = Diagonal of rectangle (d)

Ratio of Area of square to Area of rectangle = 5 : 2

Formula Used:

Diagonal of rectangle (d) = √(L2 + B2)

Area of square = s2 = d2 = L2 + B2

Area of rectangle = L × B

Calculations:

⇒ L + B = 6

⇒ (L + B)2 = 62 = 36

⇒ L2 + B2 + 2LB = 36 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Area of Square / Area of Rectangle = (L2 + B2) / LB = 5 / 2

⇒ 2(L2 + B2) = 5LB

⇒ LB = 0.4(L2 + B2)

⇒ Substitute LB in Equation 1:

⇒ (L2 + B2) + 2(0.4)(L2 + B2) = 36

⇒ (L2 + B2) + 0.8(L2 + B2) = 36

⇒ 1.8(L2 + B2) = 36

⇒ L2 + B2 = 36 ÷ 1.8

⇒ L2 + B2 = 20

⇒ Area of square = s2 = d2 = L2 + B2 = 20 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 20 cm2.

Additional Information

Properties of Rectangles and Squares

For a rectangle with sides L and B, the diagonal d = √(L2 + B2) and perimeter P = 2(L + B).

Relation between Sum and Squares

The algebraic identity (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab connects the sum of dimensions, the area of the rectangle, and the square of the diagonal.

Area of Square via Diagonal

Area of a square can be expressed as (Side)2 or (Diagonal)2 ÷ 2 if the diagonal of the square itself is given.

questions.question: The length of a side of an equilateral triangle is 8 cm. The area of the region lying between the circum – circle and the incircle of the triangle is (use : π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The length of a side of an equilateral triangle is 8 cm. The area of the region lying between the circum – circle and the incircle of the triangle is (use : π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For an equilateral triangle of side a, the area between the circumcircle and incircle is always π × (a/2)2.

Given side a = 8 cm.

Area = (22/7) × (8/2)2

Area = (22/7) × 42 = (22/7) × 16 = 352/7

Area = 50 2/7 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 50 2/7 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral triangle (a) = 8 cm

π = 22/7

Formula Used:

Circumradius (R) = a / √3

Inradius (r) = a / (2√3)

Required Area = Area of circumcircle − Area of incircle = πR2 − πr2 = π(R2 − r2)

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 8 / √3 cm

⇒ Inradius (r) = 8 / (2√3) = 4 / √3 cm

⇒ Area = π × [(8/√3)2 − (4/√3)2]

⇒ Area = π × [64/3 − 16/3]

⇒ Area = π × [48/3]

⇒ Area = π × 16

⇒ Area = (22/7) × 16 = 352/7

⇒ Area = 50 2/7 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 50 2/7 cm2.

Additional Information

Equilateral Triangle Radius Relation

For any equilateral triangle, the circumradius (R) is always double the inradius (r), i.e., R = 2r.

Area of Circles Ratio

The ratio of the area of the circumcircle to the area of the incircle in an equilateral triangle is always 4 : 1.

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The height (h) is the sum of the circumradius and inradius: h = R + r = (√3/2) × a.

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area of the triangle itself is given by (√3/4) × a2.

Thickness = External Radius (R) − Internal Radius (r) = 5 − 4 = 1 cm

∴ The correct answer is 1 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of solid sphere (rs) = 3 cm

Length of hollow cylinder (h) = 4 cm

External radius of cylinder (R) = 5 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × r3

Volume of hollow cylinder = π × h × (R2 − r2)

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of Sphere = 4/3 × π × (3)3

⇒ Volume of Sphere = 4/3 × π × 27 = 36π cm3

⇒ Volume of Hollow Cylinder = π × 4 × (52 − r2)

⇒ 36π = 4π × (25 − r2)

⇒ 36 / 4 = 25 − r2

⇒ 9 = 25 − r2

⇒ r2 = 25 − 9 = 16

⇒ r = √16 = 4 cm

⇒ Thickness of tube = External radius (R) − Internal radius (r)

⇒ Thickness = 5 cm − 4 cm = 1 cm

∴ The correct answer is 1 cm.

Additional Information

Volume of Solid Objects

For a solid sphere, Volume = 4/3 πr3. When an object is melted and reshaped, its total volume remains constant.

Hollow Cylinder Properties

Volume = πh(R2 − r2), where R is external radius and r is internal radius. Thickness = R − r.

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a solid sphere is given by 4πr2.

questions.question: If x 2 + 1/x 2 = 98 (x>0), then the value of x 3 + 1/x 3 is
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> = 98 (x>0), then the value of x<sup>3</sup> + 1/x<sup>3</sup> is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x2 + 1/x2 = a, then x + 1/x = √(a + 2).

Given x2 + 1/x2 = 98, so x + 1/x = √(98 + 2) = 10 (since x > 0).

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k.

Required value = 103 − 3(10) = 1000 − 30 = 970.

∴ The correct answer is 970.

Alternate Method

Given: x2 + 1/x2 = 98 and x > 0

Formula used: (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2 and x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 − 3(x + 1/x)

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 98 + 2

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 100

⇒ x + 1/x = √100

⇒ x + 1/x = 10

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (10)3 − 3 × (10)

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 1000 − 30

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 970

∴ The correct answer is 970.

Additional Information

Square Reciprocal Identity

For any positive x, x2 + 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)2 − 2 or (x − 1/x)2 + 2.

Cubic Reciprocal Identity

The sum of cubes is derived as x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 − 3(x + 1/x) and the difference as x3 − 1/x3 = (x − 1/x)3 + 3(x − 1/x).

Successive Higher Powers

To find x4 + 1/x4, square the value of x2 + 1/x2 and subtract 2.

questions.question: If a + 1/b = 1 and b + 1/c = 1, then the value of c + 1/a is
questions.questionHtml: If a + 1/b = 1 and b + 1/c = 1, then the value of c + 1/a is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the substitution method by picking a value for 'a' that satisfies the conditions.

Let a = 1/2.

Substitute in first eq: 1/2 + 1/b = 1 ⇒ 1/b = 1/2 ⇒ b = 2.

Substitute in second eq: 2 + 1/c = 1 ⇒ 1/c = −1 ⇒ c = −1.

Calculate: c + 1/a = −1 + 1/(1/2) = −1 + 2 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: a + 1/b = 1 and b + 1/c = 1

Formula: Express c and 1/a in terms of the same variable to find the sum.

⇒ From the first equation: a + 1/b = 1

⇒ 1/b = 1 − a

⇒ b = 1 / (1 − a)

⇒ From the second equation: b + 1/c = 1

⇒ 1/c = 1 − b

⇒ 1/c = 1 − [1 / (1 − a)]

⇒ 1/c = (1 − a − 1) / (1 − a) = −a / (1 − a)

⇒ c = (1 − a) / −a = −1/a + 1

⇒ c + 1/a = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Cyclic Symmetric Expressions

In cyclic equations of the form x + 1/y = k and y + 1/z = k, the third expression z + 1/x usually results in the same constant k.

Reciprocal Algebra

If x + 1/y = 1, then y = 1 / (1 − x). This transformation is useful for solving nested fraction problems.

Product Rule

Multiplying such cyclic equations can often simplify the expression to abc + 1 = 0 or similar identities depending on the constant.

questions.question: If x = y + z then x 3 – y 3 – z 3 is:
questions.questionHtml: If x = y + z then x<sup>3</sup>– y<sup>3</sup>– z<sup>3</sup> is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use substitution: Let y = 1 and z = 1.

Since x = y + z, then x = 1 + 1 = 2.

Calculate x3 − y3 − z3 ⇒ 23 − 13 − 13 = 8 − 1 − 1 = 6.

Check options: 3xyz = 3 × 2 × 1 × 1 = 6, which matches the result.

∴ The correct answer is 3xyz.

Alternate Method

Given: x = y + z

Formula used: (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ x = y + z

Cubing both sides:

⇒ x3 = (y + z)3

⇒ x3 = y3 + z3 + 3yz(y + z)

Substitute (y + z) = x back into the equation:

⇒ x3 = y3 + z3 + 3yz(x)

⇒ x3 = y3 + z3 + 3xyz

Rearranging the terms:

⇒ x3 − y3 − z3 = 3xyz

∴ The correct answer is 3xyz.

Additional Information

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Trinomial Cube Factorisation

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca).

Binomial Cube (Subtraction)

(a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b).

questions.question: If a + b + c + d = 4 then the value of \(\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - a} \right)\left( {1 - b} \right)\left( {1 - c} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - b} \right)\left( {1 - c} \right)\left( {1 - d} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - c} \right)\left( {1 - d} \right)\left( {1 - a} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - d} \right)\left( {1 - a} \right)\left( {1 - b} \right)}}\) is
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c + d = 4 then the value of \(\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - a} \right)\left( {1 - b} \right)\left( {1 - c} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - b} \right)\left( {1 - c} \right)\left( {1 - d} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - c} \right)\left( {1 - d} \right)\left( {1 - a} \right)}}\; + \;\frac{1}{{\left( {1 - d} \right)\left( {1 - a} \right)\left( {1 - b} \right)}}\) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume convenient values for a, b, c, and d such that their sum is 4 and no denominator becomes zero.

Let a = 4, b = 0, c = 0, and d = 0 (since 4 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 4).

Substitute these values: 1/((1 − 4)(1 − 0)(1 − 0)) + 1/((1 − 0)(1 − 0)(1 − 0)) + 1/((1 − 0)(1 − 0)(1 − 4)) + 1/((1 − 0)(1 − 4)(1 − 0))

⇒ 1/(−3) + 1/1 + 1/(−3) + 1/(−3) = −1/3 + 1 − 1/3 − 1/3 = 1 − 1 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: a + b + c + d = 4

Formula Used: Algebraic transformation and common denominator method.

Let x = (1 − a), y = (1 − b), z = (1 − c), and w = (1 − d).

⇒ x + y + z + w = (1 − a) + (1 − b) + (1 − c) + (1 − d)

⇒ x + y + z + w = 4 − (a + b + c + d)

⇒ x + y + z + w = 4 − 4 = 0

⇒ The given expression is: 1/(xyz) + 1/(yzw) + 1/(zwx) + 1/(wxy)

⇒ Taking the LCM of denominators: (w + x + y + z) / (xyzw)

⇒ Since x + y + z + w = 0, the expression becomes: 0 / (xyzw) = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Variable Substitution

In competitive math, substituting variables that satisfy the given condition (like x + y + z + w = 0) is the most efficient way to simplify complex rational expressions.

Symmetric Expressions

When terms in an expression are cyclic or symmetric, the sum often simplifies to zero or a constant based on the total sum of the individual variables.

BODMAS in Algebra

Always follow the order of operations when simplifying denominators before combining terms using a least common multiple (LCM).

questions.question: The simplified value of \(\frac{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt {12} - \sqrt {18} }} - \frac{1}{3}\; \times \;\sqrt {27} - \frac{1}{2}\; \times \;\sqrt[3]{{27}}\) is
questions.questionHtml: The simplified value of \(\frac{{\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt {12} - \sqrt {18} }} - \frac{1}{3}\; \times \;\sqrt {27} - \frac{1}{2}\; \times \;\sqrt[3]{{27}}\) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplify denominators: √12 − √18 = √6(√2 − √3) = −√6(√3 − √2).

First term: (√3 − √2) ÷ [−√6(√3 − √2)] = −1/√6.

Second term: (1/3) × √27 = (1/3) × 3√3 = √3.

Third term: (1/2) × 3√27 = (1/2) × 3 = 1.5 = 1 + 1/2.

Total = −1/√6 − √3 − 1 − 1/2 = − [ √3 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/√6 ].

∴ The correct answer is − [ √3 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/√6 ].

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = [(√3 − √2) / (√12 − √18)] − [(1/3) × √27] − [(1/2) × 3√27]

Formula/Properties Used:

√(a2b) = a√b | 3√a3 = a | Rationalization of surds.

Calculations:

⇒ Step 1: Simplify √12, √18, √27, and 3√27

⇒ √12 = √(4 × 3) = 2√3

⇒ √18 = √(9 × 2) = 3√2

⇒ √27 = √(9 × 3) = 3√3

⇒ 3√27 = 3√33 = 3

⇒ Step 2: Substitute these values into the expression

⇒ [(√3 − √2) / (2√3 − 3√2)] − [(1/3) × 3√3] − [(1/2) × 3]

⇒ Step 3: Rationalize the first term

⇒ [(√3 − √2)(2√3 + 3√2)] / [(2√3 − 3√2)(2√3 + 3√2)]

⇒ [2(3) + 3√6 − 2√6 − 3(2)] / [4(3) − 9(2)]

⇒ [6 + √6 − 6] / [12 − 18] = √6 / −6 = −1/√6

⇒ Step 4: Simplify the remaining terms

⇒ Term 2 = −√3

⇒ Term 3 = −3/2 = −(1 + 1/2)

⇒ Step 5: Combine all terms

⇒ −1/√6 − √3 − 1 − 1/2

⇒ − [ √3 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/√6 ]

∴ The correct answer is − [ √3 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/√6 ].

Additional Information

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator of the form (a − b), multiply both the numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + b) to eliminate roots using (a − b)(a + b) = a2 − b2.

Laws of Radicals

Properties like √ab = √a × √b and n√an = a are fundamental for simplifying complex expressions involving roots and powers.

BODMAS Rule

Operations must follow the order: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction for accurate results.

questions.question: If x = 11, the value of x 5 – 12x 4 + 12x 3 – 12x 2 + 12x – 1 is
questions.questionHtml: If x = 11, the value of x<sup>5</sup>– 12x<sup>4</sup> + 12x<sup>3</sup>– 12x<sup>2</sup> + 12x – 1 is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x = 11, the coefficient 12 can be written as (x + 1).

In alternating polynomials of the form xn − (x+1)xn−1 + (x+1)xn−2 ..., terms cancel out.

Expanding x5 − (x+1)x4 + (x+1)x3 − (x+1)x2 + (x+1)x − 1 leaves only the last part: x − 1.

Substitute x = 11 into the simplified result: 11 − 1 = 10.

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method

Given: x = 11

Expression: x5 − 12x4 + 12x3 − 12x2 + 12x − 1

⇒ x5 − (11 + 1)x4 + (11 + 1)x3 − (11 + 1)x2 + (11 + 1)x − 1

⇒ x5 − (x + 1)x4 + (x + 1)x3 − (x + 1)x2 + (x + 1)x − 1

⇒ x5 − x5 − x4 + x4 + x3 − x3 − x2 + x2 + x − 1

⇒ x − 1

⇒ 11 − 1 = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Additional Information

Polynomial Reduction

For a polynomial where coefficients are related to the variable as c = x ± 1, expanding the brackets leading to a telescoping sum where most terms sum to zero.

Remainder Theorem

The value of any polynomial P(x) at x = k is equivalent to the remainder when P(x) is divided by the linear factor (x − k).

Synthetic Division

This problem can also be solved by synthetic division of the coefficients [1, −12, 12, −12, 12, −1] by the root x = 11 to find the final remainder.

questions.question: If \(a = \frac{1}{{a - 5}}\) (a > 0), then the value of a + 1/a is
questions.questionHtml: If \(a = \frac{1}{{a - 5}}\)(a > 0), then the value of a + 1/a is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given equation: a = 1/(a − 5)

Rearranging gives: a(a − 5) = 1 → a − 1/a = 5

Shortcut formula: If x − 1/x = k, then x + 1/x = √(k2 + 4)

Here k = 5, so a + 1/a = √(52 + 4) = √(25 + 4) = √29

∴ The correct answer is √29.

Alternate Method

Given: a = 1/(a − 5) where a > 0

Formula Used: (x + y)2 = (x − y)2 + 4xy

⇒ a = 1/(a − 5)

⇒ a(a − 5) = 1

⇒ a2 − 5a = 1

⇒ Dividing both sides by a:

⇒ a − 5 = 1/a

⇒ a − 1/a = 5

⇒ Now, using the identity: (a + 1/a)2 = (a − 1/a)2 + 4

⇒ (a + 1/a)2 = (5)2 + 4

⇒ (a + 1/a)2 = 25 + 4 = 29

⇒ Taking square root: a + 1/a = ±√29

⇒ Since a > 0 and a − 1/a = 5 (implying a > 1/a), a + 1/a must be positive.

∴ The correct answer is √29.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Identity Relation

The relationship between the sum and difference of reciprocals is given by (x + 1/x)2 − (x − 1/x)2 = 4.

Quadratic Form Conversion

Equations of the form x + 1/x = k can be converted to quadratic form as x2 − kx + 1 = 0.

Higher Powers Shortcut

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2 and x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k.

questions.question: If a + 1/b = b + 1/c = c + 1/a (where a ≠ b ≠ c), then abc is equal to
questions.questionHtml: If a + 1/b = b + 1/c = c + 1/a (where a ≠ b ≠ c), then abc is equal to
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For cyclic expressions a + 1/b = b + 1/c = c + 1/a, the product abc is always ±1 when a, b, and c are distinct.

By subtracting terms: a − b = (b − c)/bc, b − c = (c − a)/ac, and c − a = (a − b)/ab.

Multiplying these three equations: (a − b)(b − c)(c − a) = (b − c)(c − a)(a − b) / (abc)2.

Canceling the common product (since a ≠ b ≠ c) gives (abc)2 = 1.

Thus, abc = √1 = + 1 or − 1.

∴ The correct answer is + 1 & – 1.

Alternate Method

Given: a + 1/b = b + 1/c = c + 1/a and a ≠ b ≠ c

Formula Used: Algebraic manipulation and substitution.

⇒ a + 1/b = b + 1/c

⇒ a − b = 1/c − 1/b = (b − c) / bc ... (1)

⇒ b + 1/c = c + 1/a

⇒ b − c = 1/a − 1/c = (c − a) / ac ... (2)

⇒ c + 1/a = a + 1/b

⇒ c − a = 1/b − 1/a = (a − b) / ab ... (3)

⇒ Multiply equations (1), (2), and (3):

⇒ (a − b)(b − c)(c − a) = [(b − c) × (c − a) × (a − b)] / (bc × ac × ab)

⇒ (a − b)(b − c)(c − a) = [(a − b)(b − c)(c − a)] / (a2b2c2)

⇒ Divide both sides by (a − b)(b − c)(c − a) (as a ≠ b ≠ c, product is non-zero):

⇒ 1 = 1 / (abc)2

⇒ (abc)2 = 1

⇒ abc = ±1

∴ The correct answer is + 1 & – 1.

Additional Information

Cyclic Symmetric Expressions

A cyclic expression remains invariant when variables are swapped in a specific order (a → b, b → c, c → a). In such identities, the product or sum often results in simple constants like 0, 1, or −1.

Conditional Identities

When solving cyclic equations with conditions like a ≠ b ≠ c, it allows us to divide by the differences (a − b), (b − c), and (c − a) to simplify the expression and find the value of the product abc.

Special Cases of abc = 1

If abc = 1, then the given expression a + 1/b = b + 1/c = c + 1/a reduces to a + ac = b + ab = c + bc, which is a common property in symmetric algebraic structures.

questions.question: If ax + by = 1 and bx + ay \(= \frac{{2ab}}{{{a^2}\; + \;{b^2}}}\) then (x 2 + y 2 )(a 2 + b 2 ) is equal to
questions.questionHtml: If ax + by = 1 and bx + ay \(= \frac{{2ab}}{{{a^2}\; + \;{b^2}}}\) then (x2 + y2)(a2 + b2) is equal to
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume simple values: Let a = 1 and b = 0.

Equation 1: ax + by = 1 → (1)x + (0)y = 1 ⇒ x = 1.

Equation 2: bx + ay = 2ab ÷ (a2 + b2) → (0)x + (1)y = 0 ⇒ y = 0.

Calculate the required expression: (x2 + y2)(a2 + b2) = (12 + 02)(12 + 02) = 1 × 1 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: ax + by = 1

Equation 2: bx + ay = 2ab ÷ (a2 + b2)

Calculations:

⇒ Adding Eq 1 and Eq 2: (a + b)x + (a + b)y = 1 + [2ab ÷ (a2 + b2)]

⇒ (a + b)(x + y) = (a2 + b2 + 2ab) ÷ (a2 + b2) = (a + b)2 ÷ (a2 + b2)

⇒ (x + y) = (a + b) ÷ (a2 + b2)

⇒ Subtracting Eq 2 from Eq 1: (a − b)x − (a − b)y = 1 − [2ab ÷ (a2 + b2)]

⇒ (a − b)(x − y) = (a2 + b2 − 2ab) ÷ (a2 + b2) = (a − b)2 ÷ (a2 + b2)

⇒ (x − y) = (a − b) ÷ (a2 + b2)

⇒ Using the identity: 2(x2 + y2) = (x + y)2 + (x − y)2

⇒ 2(x2 + y2) = [(a + b)2 ÷ (a2 + b2)2] + [(a − b)2 ÷ (a2 + b2)2]

⇒ 2(x2 + y2) = [(a + b)2 + (a − b)2] ÷ (a2 + b2)2 = [2(a2 + b2)] ÷ (a2 + b2)2

⇒ x2 + y2 = 1 ÷ (a2 + b2)

⇒ (x2 + y2)(a2 + b2) = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Squares

(a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2). This identity is useful for simplifying expressions involving sum and difference of terms.

Algebraic Identity for Product of Sum and Difference

(a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab. This relates the squares of sums and differences to the product of the two variables.

Method of Variable Substitution

In objective exams, setting variables to simple values like 0 or 1 is a fast way to verify or solve algebraic identities, provided the denominator does not become zero.

questions.question: If x, y, z are the three factors of a 3 – 7a – 6, then value of x + y + z will be
questions.questionHtml: If x, y, z are the three factors of a<sup>3</sup>– 7a – 6, then value of x + y + z will be
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any cubic polynomial a3 + Pa2 + Qa + R, the sum of its three linear factors is given by 3a + P.

In the expression a3 − 7a − 6, the term a2 is missing, which means the coefficient P = 0.

Sum of factors x + y + z = 3a + 0 = 3a.

∴ The correct answer is 3a.

Alternate Method

Given: x, y, and z are the factors of a3 − 7a − 6.

Formula Used: Factor Theorem − If P(k) = 0, then (a − k) is a factor of P(a).

⇒ Let P(a) = a3 − 7a − 6.

⇒ For a = −1: P(−1) = (−1)3 − 7(−1) − 6 = −1 + 7 − 6 = 0.

⇒ So, (a + 1) is a factor. Let x = a + 1.

⇒ Dividing (a3 − 7a − 6) by (a + 1) gives the quadratic (a2 − a − 6).

⇒ Factorizing the quadratic: a2 − a − 6 = a2 − 3a + 2a − 6 = a(a − 3) + 2(a − 3) = (a − 3)(a + 2).

⇒ The other two factors are y = a − 3 and z = a + 2.

⇒ x + y + z = (a + 1) + (a − 3) + (a + 2) = 3a + 1 − 3 + 2 = 3a.

∴ The correct answer is 3a.

Additional Information

Factor Theorem

A polynomial f(x) has a factor (x − k) if and only if f(k) = 0. This is useful for finding the first factor of a cubic expression via trial and error.

Vieta’s Formulas for Cubics

For a cubic equation ax3 + bx2 + cx + d = 0 with roots r1, r2, r3, the sum of roots r1 + r2 + r3 = −b/a.

Sum of Linear Factors

If a polynomial is expressed as the product of n linear factors (a − ri), their sum is na − (∑ri). For a monic cubic, this sum is 3a + (coefficient of a2).

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral of which AB is the diameter. Diagonals AC and BD intersect at E. If ∠DBC = 35°, then ∠AED measures
questions.questionHtml: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral of which AB is the diameter. Diagonals AC and BD intersect at E. If ∠DBC = 35°, then ∠AED measures
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Angle in a semicircle ∠ACB = 90°.

In ΔBCE, ∠BCE = 90° and given ∠CBE = 35°.

Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°, so ∠CEB = 180° − (90° + 35°) = 55°.

∠AED = ∠CEB (Vertically opposite angles) = 55°.

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Alternate Method

Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, AB is the diameter, and ∠DBC = 35°.

Formula: Angle in a semicircle = 90°; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

⇒ Since AB is the diameter, the angle subtended at the circumference ∠ACB = 90°.

⇒ In right-angled ΔBCE, ∠BCE = 90° and ∠CBE (or ∠DBC) = 35°.

⇒ ∠CEB = 180° − (∠BCE + ∠CBE)

⇒ ∠CEB = 180° − (90° + 35°) = 180° − 125° = 55°.

⇒ Since AC and BD are intersecting lines, ∠AED and ∠CEB are vertically opposite angles.

⇒ ∠AED = ∠CEB = 55°.

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Additional Information

Angle in a Semicircle

Any angle subtended by the diameter of a circle at its circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc or chord at the remaining part of the circle are equal; here, ∠DAC = ∠DBC = 35°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle. The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180°.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, ∠A = 70°, ∠B = 80° and O is the incentre of ΔABC. ∠ACB = 2x° and ∠BOC = y°. The values of x and y, respectively are
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle ABC, ∠A = 70°, ∠B = 80° and O is the incentre of ΔABC. ∠ACB = 2x° and ∠BOC = y°. The values of x and y, respectively are
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Angle sum of triangle: ∠C = 180° − (∠A + ∠B) = 180° − 150° = 30°.

Since ∠ACB = 2x, we have 2x = 30 ⇒ x = 15.

Incentre Property: The angle at the incentre y = 90° + ∠A/2.

y = 90° + 70°/2 = 90° + 35° = 125.

∴ The correct answer is 15, 125.

Alternate Method

Given values:

∠A = 70°

∠B = 80°

∠ACB = 2x°

∠BOC = y° (where O is the incentre)

Formula used: Sum of angles in a triangle = 180° and Incentre angle formula ∠BOC = 90° + ∠A/2.

⇒ In ΔABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 70° + 80° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 150° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 30°

⇒ Given ∠ACB = 2x, so 2x = 30 ⇒ x = 15

⇒ Now, for incentre O, ∠BOC = 90° + (∠A / 2)

⇒ y = 90° + (70° / 2)

⇒ y = 90° + 35°

⇒ y = 125

∴ The correct answer is 15, 125.

Additional Information

Incentre Definition

The incentre is the point of intersection of the internal angle bisectors of a triangle and is equidistant from all sides.

Angle at Incentre

The angle formed at the incentre by any two vertices is given by 90° + (half of the third angle). For example, ∠AOC = 90° + ∠B/2.

Excentre Angle

The angle formed by external bisectors of ∠B and ∠C at the excentre is 90° − ∠A/2.

Circumcentre Angle

The angle subtended by a side at the circumcentre is twice the angle at the opposite vertex. ∠BSC = 2 × ∠A.

questions.question: In a right – angled triangle ΔDEF, if the length of the hypotenuse EF is 12 cm, then the length of the median DX is
questions.questionHtml: In a right – angled triangle ΔDEF, if the length of the hypotenuse EF is 12 cm, then the length of the median DX is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a right-angled triangle, the length of the median drawn from the vertex of the right angle to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse.

Here, the right angle is at D (since EF is the hypotenuse) and DX is the median to EF.

Length of median DX = Hypotenuse EF ÷ 2

DX = 12 cm ÷ 2 = 6 cm

∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: In ΔDEF, ∠D = 90° and Hypotenuse EF = 12 cm.

To find: Length of the median DX, where X is the midpoint of EF.

Property: In a right-angled triangle, the midpoint of the hypotenuse is the circumcenter of the triangle.

This means XD = XE = XF = R (Circumradius).

⇒ Median DX = 1/2 × EF

⇒ DX = 1/2 × 12 cm

⇒ DX = 6 cm

∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Additional Information

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The circumradius (R) of a right-angled triangle is always equal to half of its hypotenuse. Formula: R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2.

Median Property

In any triangle, the three medians intersect at a single point called the centroid, which divides each median in a 2:1 ratio from the vertex.

Area using Medians

Area of a triangle = (4/3) × Area of a triangle formed by its three medians as sides.

questions.question: Two equal circles intersect so that their centres, and the points at which they intersect form a square of side 1 cm. The area (in sq.cm) of the portion that is common to the circles is
questions.questionHtml: Two equal circles intersect so that their centres, and the points at which they intersect form a square of side 1 cm. The area (in sq.cm) of the portion that is common to the circles is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the centers and intersection points of two equal circles form a square, the radius (r) of the circles is equal to the side of the square.

Given side of square = 1 cm → r = 1 cm.

The central angle subtended by the intersection points is 90° (property of a square).

Area of common portion = 2 × (Area of Sector − Area of Triangle) = r2(π/2 − 1).

Substituting r = 1: Area = 12 × (π/2 − 1) = π/2 − 1 sq.cm.

∴ The correct answer is π/2 − 1 sq.cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the square (s) = 1 cm.

Vertices of the square: Centers (C1, C2) and Intersection points (P, Q).

Formula:

Common Area = Area of Sector 1 + Area of Sector 2 − Area of Square

Calculations:

⇒ In square C1PC2Q, sides C1P = PC2 = C2Q = QC1 = 1 cm.

⇒ These sides represent the radii of the two circles, so r = 1 cm.

⇒ The angle at the center θ = ∠PC1Q = 90°.

⇒ Area of sector C1PQ = (90/360) × π × r2 = π/4 cm2.

⇒ Similarly, area of sector C2PQ = π/4 cm2.

⇒ Area of square C1PC2Q = side2 = 12 = 1 cm2.

⇒ Common Area = (π/4 + π/4) − 1

⇒ Common Area = π/2 − 1 sq.cm.

∴ The correct answer is π/2 − 1 sq.cm.

Additional Information

Area of a circular segment

The area of a segment is calculated as: Area = (r2/2) × [(πθ/180) − sinθ], where θ is the angle in degrees.

Intersection of two circles

The common area of two intersecting circles is twice the area of the segment formed by the common chord.

Distance between centers

In this specific case, the distance between centers C1 and C2 is the diagonal of the square, which is s√2 = √2 cm.

questions.question: PQRA is a rectangle, AP = 22 cm, PQ = 8 cm. ΔABC is a triangle whose vertices lie on the sides of PQRA such that BQ = 2 cm and QC = 16 cm, then the length of the line joining the mid points of the sides AB and BC is
questions.questionHtml: PQRA is a rectangle, AP = 22 cm, PQ = 8 cm. ΔABC is a triangle whose vertices lie on the sides of PQRA such that BQ = 2 cm and QC = 16 cm, then the length of the line joining the mid points of the sides AB and BC is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By Midpoint Theorem, the segment joining midpoints of AB and BC is equal to 1/2 × AC.

Let A = (0, 0). Then R = (8, 0) and Q = (8, 22).

Point C lies on QR such that QC = 16 cm ⇒ C = (8, 22 − 16) = (8, 6).

Using Pythagoras theorem for AC: AC = √(82 + 62) = √100 = 10 cm.

Required length = AC ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rectangle PQRA with sides AP = 22 cm and PQ = 8 cm.

Points B and C are on sides PQ and QR such that BQ = 2 cm and QC = 16 cm.

⇒ Let coordinates of vertex A be (0, 0).

⇒ Coordinates of other vertices: P(0, 22), Q(8, 22), R(8, 0).

⇒ Point B lies on PQ: B = (8 − 2, 22) = (6, 22).

⇒ Point C lies on QR: C = (8, 22 − 16) = (8, 6).

⇒ Length of AC = √((8 − 0)2 + (6 − 0)2)

⇒ AC = √(82 + 62) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 cm.

⇒ According to the Midpoint Theorem, the length of the line joining midpoints M and N of sides AB and BC is half of AC.

⇒ Length MN = AC ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Additional Information

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is exactly half its length.

Distance Formula

The distance between any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by d = √((x2−x1)2 + (y2−y1)2).

Pythagorean Triplets

For a right-angled triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, a2 + b2 = c2. Common triplets include (3, 4, 5) and (6, 8, 10).

questions.question: ΔABC is an isosceles right – angled triangle having ∠C = 90°. If D is any point on AB, then AD 2 + BD 2 is equal to
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC is an isosceles right – angled triangle having ∠C = 90°. If D is any point on AB, then AD<sup>2</sup> + BD<sup>2</sup> is equal to
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let ΔABC be an isosceles right triangle with AC = BC = 1 unit.

Then hypotenuse AB = √(12 + 12) = √2 units.

Assume D is the midpoint of AB, then AD = BD = (√2)/2 = 1/√2 units.

In a right triangle, the median to the hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse, so CD = AB/2 = (√2)/2 = 1/√2 units.

AD2 + BD2 = (1/√2)2 + (1/√2)2 = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 unit.

2CD2 = 2 × (1/√2)2 = 2 × 1/2 = 1 unit.

∴ The correct answer is 2CD2.

Alternate Method

Given: ΔABC is isosceles right-angled at C. Let AC = BC = a.

Formula: Distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) = √((x2−x1)2 + (y2−y1)2).

Let coordinates be C(0, 0), A(a, 0), and B(0, a).

The equation of line AB is x + y = a. Let D be (x, y) where y = a − x.

⇒ AD2 = (a − x)2 + (0 − y)2 = (a − x)2 + y2

⇒ Since y = a − x, AD2 = (a − x)2 + (a − x)2 = 2(a − x)2

⇒ BD2 = (x − 0)2 + (y − a)2 = x2 + (a − x − a)2 = x2 + (−x)2 = 2x2

⇒ AD2 + BD2 = 2(a − x)2 + 2x2 = 2(a2 + x2 − 2ax + x2) = 2(a2 − 2ax + 2x2)

⇒ CD2 = (x − 0)2 + (y − 0)2 = x2 + (a − x)2 = x2 + a2 + x2 − 2ax = a2 − 2ax + 2x2

⇒ Comparing the results: AD2 + BD2 = 2 × CD2

∴ The correct answer is 2CD2.

Additional Information

Median to the Hypotenuse

In any right-angled triangle, the length of the median drawn to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse.

Isosceles Right Triangle Properties

An isosceles right triangle has angles 45°, 45°, and 90°. The side ratio is always 1 : 1 : √2.

Apollonius Theorem

For any triangle ABC and median AD, AB2 + AC2 = 2(AD2 + BD2). This relates sides to the median.

questions.question: D and E are points on the sides AB and AC respectively of ΔABC such that DE is parallel to BC and AD : DB = 4 : 5, CD and BE intersect each other at F. Then the ratio of the areas of ΔDEF and ΔCBF
questions.questionHtml: D and E are points on the sides AB and AC respectively of ΔABC such that DE is parallel to BC and AD : DB = 4 : 5, CD and BE intersect each other at F. Then the ratio of the areas of ΔDEF and ΔCBF
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio AD : AB = AD : (AD + DB) = 4 : (4 + 5) = 4 : 9.

Since DE ∥ BC, ΔADE ∼ ΔABC ⇒ DE/BC = AD/AB = 4/9.

Also, ΔDEF ∼ ΔCBF (by AA similarity property for triangles between parallel lines).

Ratio of Areas = (Ratio of corresponding sides)2 = (4/9)2 = 16 : 81.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 81.

Alternate Method

Given: AD : DB = 4 : 5 and DE ∥ BC.

Formula Used: Area ratio of similar triangles = (Side ratio)2.

⇒ Let AD = 4x and DB = 5x. Then AB = AD + DB = 9x.

⇒ In ΔADE and ΔABC, DE ∥ BC, so ΔADE ∼ ΔABC (by AA similarity).

⇒ DE/BC = AD/AB = 4x / 9x = 4/9.

⇒ In ΔDEF and ΔCBF:

⇒ ∠EDF = ∠BCF (Alternate interior angles as DE ∥ BC)

⇒ ∠DEF = ∠CBF (Alternate interior angles as DE ∥ BC)

⇒ ∴ ΔDEF ∼ ΔCBF (by AA similarity criterion).

⇒ Area(ΔDEF) / Area(ΔCBF) = (DE / BC)2

⇒ Area Ratio = (4 / 9)2 = 16 / 81.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 81.

Additional Information

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

Area Theorem for Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area1/Area2 = (s1/s2)2.

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar by the AA (Angle-Angle) similarity rule.

questions.question: Diagonals of a trapezium ABCD with AB II CD intersect each other at the point O. If AB = 2CD, then the ratio of the areas of ΔAOB and ΔCOD is
questions.questionHtml: Diagonals of a trapezium ABCD with AB II CD intersect each other at the point O. If AB = 2CD, then the ratio of the areas of ΔAOB and ΔCOD is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a trapezium with AB || CD, ΔAOB and ΔCOD are always similar.

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Given side ratio AB : CD = 2 : 1.

Area ratio = (Side Ratio)2 = (2/1)2 = 4/1.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 1.

Alternate Method

Given: ABCD is a trapezium where AB || CD and AB = 2CD. O is the intersection point of diagonals AC and BD.

In ΔAOB and ΔCOD:

⇒ ∠OAB = ∠OCD (Alternate interior angles as AB || CD)

⇒ ∠OBA = ∠ODC (Alternate interior angles as AB || CD)

⇒ ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (By AA similarity criterion)

According to the property of similar triangles:

⇒ Area(ΔAOB) ÷ Area(ΔCOD) = (AB ÷ CD)2

⇒ Area(ΔAOB) ÷ Area(ΔCOD) = (2CD ÷ CD)2 [Since AB = 2CD]

⇒ Area(ΔAOB) ÷ Area(ΔCOD) = (2 ÷ 1)2

⇒ Area(ΔAOB) ÷ Area(ΔCOD) = 4 ÷ 1

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 1.

Additional Information

Area Property of Similar Triangles

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians. Area1/Area2 = (s1/s2)2.

Trapezium Diagonal Property

In any trapezium, the triangles formed by the non-parallel sides and the intersection of diagonals have equal area. Area(ΔAOD) = Area(ΔBOC).

Area of Trapezium

The total area of a trapezium is given by 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × height = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

questions.question: If O is the orthocentre of ΔABC and ∠BOC = 100°, the measure of ∠BAC is
questions.questionHtml: If O is the orthocentre of ΔABC and ∠BOC = 100°, the measure of ∠BAC is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In any triangle, the angle formed by the orthocentre at the base side is supplementary to the opposite vertex angle.

Property: ∠BOC + ∠BAC = 180°

Given: ∠BOC = 100°

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 100° = 80°

∴ The correct answer is 80°.

Alternate Method

Given:

O is the orthocentre of △ABC

∠BOC = 100°

Formula Used:

∠BOC = 180° − ∠BAC

Calculation:

⇒ 100° = 180° − ∠BAC

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 100°

⇒ ∠BAC = 80°

∴ ∠BAC = 80°.

Additional Information

Circumcentre Angle Property

If O is the circumcentre of ΔABC, then the angle subtended at the centre is double the angle at the circumference: ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC.

Incentre Angle Property

If I is the incentre of ΔABC, the angle BOC is given by the formula: ∠BIC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2).

Excentre Angle Property

If E is the excentre opposite to vertex A, the angle formed is: ∠BEC = 90° − (∠A ÷ 2).

questions.question: If secA + tanA = a, then the value of cosA is
questions.questionHtml: If secA + tanA = a, then the value of cosA is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If secA + tanA = a, then secA − tanA = 1/a based on the identity sec2A − tan2A = 1.

Adding the two equations: (secA + tanA) + (secA − tanA) = a + 1/a

2 secA = (a2 + 1) / a ⇒ secA = (a2 + 1) / 2a

Since cosA = 1/secA, then cosA = 2a / (a2 + 1).

∴ The correct answer is 2a / (a2 + 1).

Alternate Method

Given: secA + tanA = a

Formula Used: sec2A − tan2A = 1 and cosA = 1/secA

⇒ We know that sec2A − tan2A = 1

⇒ (secA + tanA)(secA − tanA) = 1

⇒ a × (secA − tanA) = 1

⇒ secA − tanA = 1/a

⇒ Adding (secA + tanA = a) and (secA − tanA = 1/a):

⇒ 2 secA = a + 1/a

⇒ 2 secA = (a2 + 1) / a

⇒ secA = (a2 + 1) / 2a

⇒ cosA = 1 / secA

⇒ cosA = 2a / (a2 + 1)

∴ The correct answer is 2a / (a2 + 1).

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental identity is sec2θ − tan2θ = 1, which leads to (secθ + tanθ) = 1 / (secθ − tanθ).

Finding tanA

By subtracting the two equations instead of adding, we get 2 tanA = a − 1/a, so tanA = (a2 − 1) / 2a.

Cosecant and Cotangent Relation

Similarly, cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1. If cosecA + cotA = k, then cosecA = (k2 + 1) / 2k and cotA = (k2 − 1) / 2k.

questions.question: If sin P + cosec P = 2, then the value of sin 7 P + cosec 7 P is
questions.questionHtml: If sin P + cosec P = 2, then the value of sin<sup>7</sup>P + cosec<sup>7</sup>P is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If the sum of a trigonometric ratio and its reciprocal (like sin P and cosec P) is 2, then the value of each term must be 1.

Here, sin P + cosec P = 2 → sin P = 1 and cosec P = 1.

Any positive power of 1 is always 1.

∴ sin7P + cosec7P = 17 + 17 = 1 + 1 = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given: sin P + cosec P = 2

Formula Used: cosec P = 1 / sin P

⇒ sin P + 1 / sin P = 2

⇒ (sin2P + 1) / sin P = 2

⇒ sin2P + 1 = 2 sin P

⇒ sin2P − 2 sin P + 1 = 0

⇒ (sin P − 1)2 = 0

⇒ sin P = 1

⇒ cosec P = 1 / sin P = 1 / 1 = 1

⇒ sin7P + cosec7P = (1)7 + (1)7

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios

Pairs like (sin θ, cosec θ), (cos θ, sec θ), and (tan θ, cot θ) are reciprocals; their product is always 1.

Algebraic Identity x + 1/x

If x + 1/x = 2, then x = 1. This implies xn + 1/xn = 2 for any power n.

Maximum/Minimum Values

For positive values, the minimum value of (x + 1/x) is 2, occurring when x = 1.

questions.question: If cosx.cosy + sinx.siny = – 1 then cosx + cosy is
questions.questionHtml: If cosx.cosy + sinx.siny = – 1 then cosx + cosy is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The given expression cos x cos y + sin x sin y = −1 is the identity for cos(x − y).

Thus, cos(x − y) = −1, which implies the phase difference between x and y is 180° (π radians).

Using the sum-to-product formula: cos x + cos y = 2 cos((x + y)/2) cos((x − y)/2).

Substitute (x − y)/2 = 90° (π/2): cos x + cos y = 2 cos((x + y)/2) × cos(90°).

Since cos 90° = 0, the entire expression becomes 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: cos x cos y + sin x sin y = −1

Formula Used: cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B

⇒ cos(x − y) = −1

⇒ x − y = π (as cos π = −1)

⇒ x = π + y

⇒ cos x = cos(π + y)

⇒ cos x = −cos y (Since cos(π + θ) = −cos θ)

⇒ cos x + cos y = −cos y + cos y

⇒ cos x + cos y = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Sum to Product Formulas

cos A + cos B = 2 cos((A+B)/2) cos((A−B)/2) and cos A − cos B = −2 sin((A+B)/2) sin((A−B)/2).

Cosine Angle Difference Identity

cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B. If this equals −1, the angles are separated by π, 3π, etc.

Quadrantal Angles

cos(0) = 1, cos(π/2) = 0, cos(π) = −1, and cos(3π/2) = 0. These are essential for solving trigonometric equations.

questions.question: The value of the expression 2(sin 6 θ + cos 6 θ) – 3(sin 4 θ + cos 4 θ) + 1 is
questions.questionHtml: The value of the expression 2(sin<sup>6</sup>θ + cos<sup>6</sup>θ) – 3(sin<sup>4</sup>θ + cos<sup>4</sup>θ) + 1 is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the expression is independent of θ, we can substitute any standard value for θ.

Let θ = 0°.

Then sin 0° = 0 and cos 0° = 1.

Substitute these values into the expression: 2(06 + 16) − 3(04 + 14) + 1

⇒ 2(1) − 3(1) + 1 = 2 − 3 + 1 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: 2(sin6θ + cos6θ) − 3(sin4θ + cos4θ) + 1

Formula Used:

1. sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

2. a2 + b2 = (a + b)2 − 2ab

3. a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 − 3ab(a + b)

⇒ sin4θ + cos4θ = (sin2θ)2 + (cos2θ)2 = (sin2θ + cos2θ)2 − 2sin2θcos2θ = 1 − 2sin2θcos2θ

⇒ sin6θ + cos6θ = (sin2θ)3 + (cos2θ)3 = (sin2θ + cos2θ)3 − 3sin2θcos2θ(sin2θ + cos2θ) = 1 − 3sin2θcos2θ

⇒ Expression = 2(1 − 3sin2θcos2θ) − 3(1 − 2sin2θcos2θ) + 1

⇒ = 2 − 6sin2θcos2θ − 3 + 6sin2θcos2θ + 1

⇒ = 2 − 3 + 1 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

The three basic Pythagorean identities are: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Power Reduction Identities

Higher powers like sin4θ + cos4θ and sin6θ + cos6θ can always be expressed in terms of (sin2θ + cos2θ) using algebraic expansions.

Value Substitution Method

For any trigonometric expression that is independent of the angle θ, substituting standard angles like 0°, 45°, or 90° will yield the constant result quickly.

questions.question: If \(\cos \theta = \frac{{{x^2} - {y^2}}}{{{x^2}\; + \;{y^2}}}\) then the value of cot θ is equal to [If 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°]
questions.questionHtml: If \(\cos \theta = \frac{{{x^2} - {y^2}}}{{{x^2}\; + \;{y^2}}}\) then the value of cot θ is equal to [If 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°]
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Recognize the standard Pythagorean triplet for expressions: (x2 − y2), 2xy, and (x2 + y2).

Given cos θ = (x2 − y2) / (x2 + y2), which corresponds to Base / Hypotenuse.

In this triplet, the remaining side (Perpendicular) must be 2xy.

We know that cot θ = Base ÷ Perpendicular.

∴ cot θ = (x2 − y2) / 2xy.

∴ The correct answer is (x2 − y2) / 2xy.

Alternate Method

Given: cos θ = (x2 − y2) / (x2 + y2)

Formula: In a right-angled triangle, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse and cot θ = Base / Perpendicular.

⇒ Base (B) = x2 − y2

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = x2 + y2

⇒ According to Pythagoras theorem: P2 + B2 = H2

⇒ P2 = (x2 + y2)2 − (x2 − y2)2

⇒ P2 = (x4 + y4 + 2x2y2) − (x4 + y4 − 2x2y2)

⇒ P2 = 4x2y2

⇒ P = √(4x2y2) = 2xy

⇒ cot θ = Base / Perpendicular

⇒ cot θ = (x2 − y2) / 2xy

∴ The correct answer is (x2 − y2) / 2xy.

Additional Information

Standard Algebraic Pythagorean Triplets

For any two numbers x and y, the sides (x2 − y2), 2xy, and (x2 + y2) always form a right-angled triangle where the hypotenuse is the largest side, (x2 + y2).

Trigonometric Ratio Identities

cot θ = cos θ / sin θ. Since sin θ = P/H = 2xy / (x2 + y2), then cot θ = [(x2 − y2)/(x2 + y2)] ÷ [2xy/(x2 + y2)] = (x2 − y2) / 2xy.

Fundamental Identity

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1. This identity can be used to find sin θ if cos θ is known, and subsequently cot θ can be calculated.

questions.question: The distance between two pillars is 120 metres. The height of one pillar is thrice the other. The angles of elevation of their tops from the midpoint of the line connecting their feet are complementary to each other. The height (in metres) of the taller pillar is (Use: √3 = 1.732)

The angles of elevation of their tops from the midpoint of the line connecting their feet are complementary to each other. The height (in metres) of the taller pillar is (Use: √3 = 1.732)

Midpoint distance from each pillar = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 m.

Let the shorter height be h and taller height be 3h.

h = 20√3. Taller height = 3h = 60√3 m.

Height = 60 × 1.732 = 103.92 m.

∴ The correct answer is 103.92 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance between pillars = 120 m

Height of taller pillar = 3 × Height of shorter pillar

Observation point = Midpoint of 120 m line

Formula Used:

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base; tan (90° − θ) = cot θ

Let height of shorter pillar = h and height of taller pillar = 3h.

Distance of midpoint from each pillar = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 m.

⇒ In first triangle: tan θ = h / 60

⇒ In second triangle: tan (90° − θ) = 3h / 60

⇒ cot θ = 3h / 60

⇒ tan θ × cot θ = (h / 60) × (3h / 60)

⇒ 1 = 3h2 / 3600

⇒ 3h2 = 3600 ⇒ h2 = 1200

⇒ h = √(400 × 3) = 20√3 m

⇒ Height of taller pillar = 3h = 3 × 20√3 = 60√3 m

⇒ Height = 60 × 1.732 = 103.92 m

∴ The correct answer is 103.92 m.

Additional Information

Complementary Angles Property

If angles of elevation from a point are complementary (θ and 90°−θ), their product tan θ × tan(90°−θ) equals 1.

Standard Result for Heights

When observing a single tower of height H from two points at distances a and b such that angles are complementary, H = √(ab).

Trigonometric Ratios

tan θ = Perpendicular/Base, cot θ = Base/Perpendicular, and tan θ = 1/cot θ.

questions.question: If x = cosecθ – sinθ and y = secθ – cosθ, then the relation between x and y is
questions.questionHtml: If x = cosecθ – sinθ and y = secθ – cosθ, then the relation between x and y is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put θ = 45° to check the relation directly.

x = cosec 45° − sin 45° = √2 − 1/√2 = 1/√2

y = sec 45° − cos 45° = √2 − 1/√2 = 1/√2

Substitute in x2y2(x2 + y2 + 3): (1/2) × (1/2) × (1/2 + 1/2 + 3) = 1/4 × 4 = 1.

This matches the condition in Option 2.

∴ The correct answer is x2y2(x2 + y2 + 3) = 1.

Alternate Method

Given: x = cosecθ − sinθ and y = secθ − cosθ

Formula Used: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 and (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ x = (1/sinθ) − sinθ = (1 − sin2θ)/sinθ = cos2θ/sinθ

⇒ y = (1/cosθ) − cosθ = (1 − cos2θ)/cosθ = sin2θ/cosθ

⇒ x2 = cos4θ/sin2θ and y2 = sin4θ/cos2θ

⇒ x2y2 = (cos4θ/sin2θ) × (sin4θ/cos2θ) = sin2θcos2θ

⇒ x2 + y2 + 3 = (cos4θ/sin2θ) + (sin4θ/cos2θ) + 3

⇒ x2 + y2 + 3 = (cos6θ + sin6θ + 3sin2θcos2θ) / (sin2θcos2θ)

⇒ Since sin6θ + cos6θ + 3sin2θcos2θ = (sin2θ + cos2θ)3 = 1

⇒ x2 + y2 + 3 = 1 / (sin2θcos2θ)

⇒ x2y2(x2 + y2 + 3) = (sin2θcos2θ) × (1 / (sin2θcos2θ)) = 1

∴ The correct answer is x2y2(x2 + y2 + 3) = 1.

Additional Information

Fundamental Identity

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 is the most basic trigonometric identity derived from the Pythagorean theorem.

Higher Power Identities

sin4θ + cos4θ = 1 − 2sin2θcos2θ and sin6θ + cos6θ = 1 − 3sin2θcos2θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosecθ = 1/sinθ and secθ = 1/cosθ. These are used to simplify expressions involving differences of ratios.

questions.question: A hydrogen filled balloon ascending at the rate of 18 kmph was drifted by wind. Its angle of elevation at 10 th and 15 th minutes were found to be 60° and 45° respectively. The wind speed (in whole numbers) during the last five minutes, approximately, is equal to
questions.questionHtml: A hydrogen filled balloon ascending at the rate of 18 kmph was drifted by wind. Its angle of elevation at 10<sup>th</sup> and 15<sup>th</sup> minutes were found to be 60° and 45° respectively. The wind speed (in whole numbers) during the last five minutes, approximately, is equal to
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Vertical speed = 18 kmph. Height at 10 min = 3 km; Height at 15 min = 4.5 km.

Horizontal distance at 10 min (60°) = 3 ÷ √3 = 1.732 km.

Horizontal distance at 15 min (45°) = 4.5 ÷ 1 = 4.5 km.

Wind drift in 5 mins = 4.5 − 1.732 = 2.768 km.

Wind speed = 2.768 × (60 ÷ 5) = 2.768 × 12 = 33.216 ≈ 33 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 33 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ascent rate of balloon = 18 km/hr

Time 1 (t1) = 10 min | Angle (θ1) = 60°

Time 2 (t2) = 15 min | Angle (θ2) = 45°

Formula:

Distance = Speed × Time | Tan θ = Height ÷ Horizontal Distance

Calculations:

⇒ Height at 10 min (h1) = 18 × (10 ÷ 60) = 3 km

⇒ Horizontal Distance at 10 min (x1) = h1 ÷ tan 60° = 3 ÷ √3 = √3 ≈ 1.732 km

⇒ Height at 15 min (h2) = 18 × (15 ÷ 60) = 4.5 km

⇒ Horizontal Distance at 15 min (x2) = h2 ÷ tan 45° = 4.5 ÷ 1 = 4.5 km

⇒ Horizontal Drift (last 5 min) = x2 − x1 = 4.5 − 1.732 = 2.768 km

⇒ Time Interval = 5 minutes = 5 ÷ 60 = 1 ÷ 12 hours

⇒ Wind Speed = Drift ÷ Time = 2.768 ÷ (1 ÷ 12) = 2.768 × 12 = 33.216 km/hr

⇒ Approximate whole number = 33 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 33 km/hr.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios in Heights and Distances

Tan θ = Opposite (Height) ÷ Adjacent (Base). Common values: Tan 30° = 1/√3, Tan 45° = 1, Tan 60° = √3.

Speed, Distance, and Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time. When time is in minutes, divide by 60 to convert it into hours for km/hr calculations.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. As the object moves further away horizontally, the angle of elevation decreases for the same height.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of an aeroplane as observed from a point 30 m above the transparent water – surface of a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of the image of the aeroplane in the water of the lake is 60°. The height of the aeroplane from the water – surface of the lake is
questions.questionHtml: The angle of elevation of an aeroplane as observed from a point 30 m above the transparent water – surface of a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of the image of the aeroplane in the water of the lake is 60°. The height of the aeroplane from the water – surface of the lake is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Height of plane from surface (H) = h × [(tan θ2 + tan θ1) ÷ (tan θ2 − tan θ1)]

Here, h = 30 m, θ1 (elevation) = 30°, and θ2 (depression) = 60°.

H = 30 × [(√3 + 1/√3) ÷ (√3 − 1/√3)]

H = 30 × [(4/√3) ÷ (2/√3)] = 30 × (4 ÷ 2) = 60 m.

∴ The correct answer is 60 m.

Alternate Method

Given: Height of observation point (h) = 30 m; Angle of elevation (θ1) = 30°; Angle of depression of image (θ2) = 60°.

Formula: tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base; In reflection, Height of Object above water = Depth of Image below water.

Let H be the height of the aeroplane from the water surface.

Vertical height above observation level = H − 30.

Vertical depth of image below observation level = H + 30.

Let the horizontal distance from the observation point to the plane be x.

⇒ In Δ Elevation: tan 30° = (H − 30) ÷ x

⇒ x = (H − 30) × √3 — (Eq 1)

⇒ In Δ Depression: tan 60° = (H + 30) ÷ x

⇒ x = (H + 30) ÷ √3 — (Eq 2)

⇒ Equating x from Eq 1 and Eq 2: (H − 30) × √3 = (H + 30) ÷ √3

⇒ 3(H − 30) = H + 30

⇒ 3H − 90 = H + 30

⇒ 2H = 120

⇒ H = 60 m

∴ The correct answer is 60 m.

Additional Information

Reflection in Water

In physics and trigonometry, the height of an object above a horizontal reflecting surface is exactly equal to the depth of its image below that surface.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal, while the angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal.

Important Trigonometric Ratios

tan 30° = 1/√3; tan 45° = 1; tan 60° = √3. These are frequently used in height and distance problems.

questions.question: The angles of depression of two ships from the top of a light house are 60° and 45° towards east. If the ships are 300 m apart, the height of the light house is
questions.questionHtml: The angles of depression of two ships from the top of a light house are 60° and 45° towards east. If the ships are 300 m apart, the height of the light house is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two objects on the same side of a tower of height h, the distance between them is d = h(cot θ1 − cot θ2), where θ1 is the smaller angle.

Here, d = 300 m, θ1 = 45°, and θ2 = 60°.

300 = h(cot 45° − cot 60°) ⇒ 300 = h(1 − 1/√3)

h = (300 × √3) / (√3 − 1) ⇒ h = [300√3(√3 + 1)] / [( √3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

h = (900 + 300√3) / 2 = 450 + 150√3 = 150(3 + √3) m

∴ The correct answer is 150(3 + √3) meter.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance between ships (CD) = 300 m

Angle of depression (and elevation) to Ship 1 (∠ACB) = 45°

Angle of depression (and elevation) to Ship 2 (∠ADB) = 60°

Height of light house (AB) = h

In right ▵ABD:

⇒ tan 60° = AB / BD

⇒ √3 = h / x

⇒ x = h / √3 ---- (1)

In right ▵ABC:

⇒ tan 45° = AB / BC

⇒ 1 = h / (x + 300)

⇒ h = x + 300

Substitute value of x from (1):

⇒ h = (h / √3) + 300

⇒ h − (h / √3) = 300

⇒ h(√3 − 1) / √3 = 300

⇒ h = 300√3 / (√3 − 1)

Rationalizing the denominator:

⇒ h = [300√3 × (√3 + 1)] / [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = [300(3 + √3)] / (3 − 1)

⇒ h = 300(3 + √3) / 2

⇒ h = 150(3 + √3)

∴ The correct answer is 150(3 + √3) meter.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. These values are essential for solving height and distance problems involving right-angled triangles.

Angle of Depression vs Elevation

The angle of depression from the top is numerically equal to the angle of elevation from the object to the top because they are alternate interior angles between parallel lines.

Distance Formula for Height

When two points are on the same side of a tower: d = h(cot θsmall − cot θlarge). When they are on opposite sides: d = h(cot θ1 + cot θ2).
